Cc: julie.singer@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: KPI readout pre-brief: OKR checkpoints + QBR prep (latency, cost, uptime, usage)

Team — attaching the consolidated monthly dashboard ahead of tonight's leadership pre-brief. I focused the deck on the four asks we agreed on: latency distribution, service unit cost, uptime incidents, and customer usage patterns that map back to our OKRs. Key points at a glance:

- Latency: p50 = 42ms (flat), p95 = 310ms (up from 230ms last month, correlated with longer seq lengths on Hosted API).
- Cost: estimate = $1,920 per 1M tokens after caching improvements; raw inference compute costs down 8% MoM but cache miss rate increased 6%.
- Uptime: 99.95% last 30 days, two regional incidents (EU zone B) accounted for 18 minutes total; auto-failover executed but we need a postmortem action item.
- Usage: active routes grew 14% MoM; majority of growth in generation routes from two enterprise customers (Acme & Skyline).

Primary asks for the pre-brief:
1) Ira/Connor: confirm if we can push the new KV cache TTL tweak to Dedicated tomorrow; if not, call out rollback plan.
2) Laura: quick slide on cost-per-1M token sensitivity to batching threshold change (+/- 10%).
3) Ops: short incident timeline and whether compensating credits will be needed for Acme.

Attachments: kpi-dashboard-march-2029.pdf (high-level charts), okrs-tracker-2029-q1.xlsx (owners + progress).

I'll be in the pre-brief at 4pm PT — please reply with owner confirmations and any blockers by noon so I can fold into the readout.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Mar 2029 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KPI readout pre-brief: OKR checkpoints + QBR prep (latency, cost, uptime, usage)

Marissa — quick update on the KV cache TTL tweak. Devs ran a canary last night on Dedicated pool cluster-03: miss rate dropped 4% and average token latency dropped ~9% for sequences >1k. We found one regression in the compaction path that could increase tail latency under sustained spike; patch ready but requires a short restart window.

Propose: deploy the TTL tweak to Dedicated tomorrow in a staged rollout (cluster-03 -> cluster-01 -> remaining clusters) with a 30-minute maintenance window for each cluster. If leadership prefers zero restarts, we can delay but expect p95 to stay elevated.

I'll own the rollout and will post status in #dedicated-rollout.

Connor
Sr. Engineering Manager — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Adding a short cost sensitivity slide — draft numbers below. Will attach before noon.

Cost sensitivity (baseline = $1,920 / 1M tokens):
- Increase batching threshold by +20% -> cost down ~11% but latency p95 +10ms on short sequences (<64 tokens).
- Aggressive quantization on non-critical routes -> cost down additional 6%, possible small quality drift on low-frequency prompt types.
- Caching improvement (Connor's rollout) -> projected effective cost down 9% due to lower cache misses on long sequences.

Action: recommend we present two options to leadership: (A) immediate TTL rollout + conservative batching tweaks (preferred); (B) postpone TTL for a no-restart plan and accept current p95 risk.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Economics
Redwood Inference
